stories.label: New Zealand preliminary vote leaves unclear who will govern
stories.summary: Preliminary results give Christopher Luxon's National-led coalition a slim majority with about 14% of votes (special votes) still uncounted, so New Zealand waits weeks for a government. Lead with the margin and the uncounted share; explain how special votes have shifted seats in past MMP elections and which partner (ACT, NZ First) holds the leverage. Fills the Oceania gap flagged by the daily audit.

stories.label: Two tankers explode, burn in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: New since the 11-06 and 11-07 coverage: the IRGC Navy says two more tankers on an 'unauthorized route' struck mines overnight and are burning, UKMTO logged a fresh incident with a bulk carrier 18nm off Khorfakkan, explosions were heard again on Qeshm, and Iran's army says Hormuz stays closed. The claim of mines and 'violating' ships is the IRGC's, via Iranian and Russian state media — attribute it. Lead with Iran running a permit regime by mine: ships either take Tehran's route or risk the minefield. Chart ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude.

stories.label: Pakistan's Hormuz agreement with Iran faces test after LNG tanker attack
stories.summary: Pakistan negotiated its own safe-passage understanding with Tehran, yet a Pakistan-bound LNG carrier (Qatari gas) was attacked. The mechanism: Pakistan imports most of its LNG from Qatar through Hormuz, so a bilateral deal with Iran was its only hedge, and it just failed. Lead with what the country's power and fertilizer plants depend on, and the push to diversify gas suppliers. Chart natural gas and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: Canary Islands' El Hierro declares emergency amid migrant, refugee influx
stories.summary: More than 3,300 people reached El Hierro — an island of about 11,000 — by boat in the first week of November, and its authorities declared an emergency and asked Madrid for help. Lead with the ratio. The structural why: the Atlantic route from Senegal, Mauritania and Mali is the deadliest into Europe, and it swells when Mediterranean routes close. Name who is fleeing and from what, not just the arrivals count.

stories.label: Bomb-laden drone attack on a military base in Colombia! 5 soldiers killed
stories.summary: Explosive-laden drones hit a military base in Santa Rosa del Sur, Bolívar, killing 5 soldiers and wounding 33 (8 seriously). Lead with the toll and the weapon: Colombia's armed groups (ELN and Gulf Clan factions contest southern Bolívar's gold-mining zone) now use the cheap drone warfare seen in Ukraine and Sudan. Name the suspected group only if the authorities do.

stories.label: Saudi raids leave 1,039 dead, wounded in Yemen
stories.summary: New figure since the 11-07 Sanaa-strike story: Yemen's (Sanaa-based) health minister puts the toll of Saudi strikes since July 13 at 1,039 killed or wounded, with bodies still being pulled from homes in Bani Hushaysh, Sanaa province. Attribute the count to the Houthi-run ministry via Iranian state media. Lead with the cumulative toll on civilians — the escalation of the Saudi-Houthi front is the story the daily audit is watching.

stories.label: Govt urged to pursue review of FCC verdict on workplace harassment laws
stories.summary: Pakistan's new Federal Constitutional Court read workplace-harassment law narrowly, and a National Assembly committee now presses the government to pursue its review petition. Lead with what the ruling removes — which conduct and which workers fall outside protection — and the precedent: the FCC, created by the 27th Amendment, is reshaping rights law within its first year.

stories.label: 'Special master' named for ethics probe in lawsuit over Trump's DC golf project
stories.summary: A federal judge will appoint a former top federal prosecutor to investigate whether Justice Department lawyers committed ethical violations defending Trump's plan to close and renovate a historic public golf course in Washington (Reuters). Lead with the rare step: a court probing the government's own lawyers' conduct. The accountability mechanism is the story, not the golf.

stories.label: 中国白酒出口韩国暴涨85%，谁在买？
stories.summary: Chinese baijiu exports to South Korea jumped 85%, while the liquor sells weakly at home. Lead with the number and who is buying — Korean drinkers mixing it, Chinese diaspora, tourism — and the mechanism: distillers facing a domestic slump turning to export markets, as China's wider consumer weakness pushes producers abroad.

stories.label: Why the tropics lose the most birds when cities expand
stories.summary: A new study finds urban expansion strips the most bird diversity in the tropics, where species are most numerous and most specialized. Lead with the size of the loss and the mechanism (narrow niches, little tolerance for cities), and the stakes: most of the world's urban growth to 2050 is in tropical Africa and Asia. Name the journal.

stories.label: US military looks to curb Iranian land commerce
stories.summary: The US blockade of Iran widens from sea to land: CENTCOM announced a task force to choke Iran's commerce across its land borders and the Caspian Sea, and the same day a US aircraft fired on and disabled a St Kitts and Nevis-flagged cargo ship leaving an Iranian port in the Gulf of Oman. Lead with the disabled ship as proof the blockade is now enforced by fire on civilian vessels, then the land task force as the admission the naval blockade has not cut Iran off (Mehr calls it a response to failure). Who pays: Iran's neighbours on the overland routes (Iraq, Turkmenistan, the Caspian states) and seafarers. Chart ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz; Iran's army says Hormuz stays closed.

stories.label: Syria rebuffs reports of sending troops to Yemen
stories.summary: New development since the Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia: Saudi-led air strikes hit Sanaa and killed at least 27 people, the Houthis say, while Yemeni government forces report ground advances. Lead with the dead in Sanaa, the escalation of a war that had been in truce. Then Damascus: Syria denies sending troops but says its training pact with Riyadh 'could eventually lead to a mutual defence agreement', which would pull post-Assad Syria into the Saudi camp. Do not repeat the 11-06 story on Syrian military advisers.

stories.label: France sees new round of Yellow Vest, student protests
stories.summary: About 146,000 people marched across France for a fourth straight weekend against the cost of living, with tear gas in Paris and Lyon. Lead with the number and the cause: energy prices driven up by the Iran war, which the EU puts at €127bn in extra fossil-fuel costs, landing on French households. Distinct from the Mélenchon rally story: this is the street, students and Yellow Vests, not one party.

stories.label: Trump orders DOJ to investigate Democrats for 'threatening' people
stories.summary: Days after losing Congress, Trump publicly ordered the Justice Department to investigate Democrats, accusing them of threatening people, and urged donors to report 'threats'. Lead with the order itself: a president directing prosecutors at the opposition by social-media post. The mechanism is the DOJ's independence; the stake is what a lame-duck White House does with prosecutorial power before the new Congress sits. Do not repeat the Miller or Hegseth stories.

stories.label: Heavy rains flood more than 70,000 tents in refugee camps across Gaza
stories.summary: The first heavy winter rain flooded more than 70,000 tents in Gaza's displacement camps, with casualties reported and civil defence evacuating families, per Gaza authorities quoted by Maan and carried by Russian state agency TASS (attribute accordingly). Lead with the 70,000 tents: the people in them are there because their homes were destroyed and rebuilding materials are restricted, so this is a consequence of siege, not weather. File as politics, not science.

stories.label: ANC faces coalition scramble after electoral rout as control of key metros slips away
stories.summary: New development beyond the 11-06 ActionSA township story: with final local-election results in, the ANC has lost control of key metros (eThekwini, Ekurhuleni, Buffalo City) and councils must convene within 14 days. Lead with the clock and the choice: coalition deals, opposition benches, or uneasy partnerships. The structural point is the end of one-party control of South Africa's cities and who will run water, power and budgets for millions.

stories.label: Japan manufacturers lift profit outlooks on price hikes, weak yen
stories.summary: Nearly half of Japan's listed manufacturers raised net profit forecasts for the year to March 2027, on price hikes, AI investment and the weak yen. Lead with who wins and who pays: exporters book currency gains while Japanese households pay more for imported energy and food. Chart the yen.

stories.label: COP31: What Nigeria, other African countries will push for at UN climate summit
stories.summary: Ahead of COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, the African Group of Negotiators sets its demands: more climate finance and an ambitious adaptation goal. Lead with the money gap: the continent that emitted least pays most for adaptation, and pledged finance has not arrived. Name the specific figures the AGN asks for and who is expected to pay.

stories.label: Binance users in some European countries told to pull crypto before fees kick in, with accounts closing by year end
stories.summary: The world's largest crypto exchange still has no MiCA licence, so it is telling users in some EU countries (France, Portugal among them) to withdraw before monthly fees start on 29 November, with accounts closing at year end. Lead with the regulation working as designed: the EU's licensing regime is pushing out an exchange that would not comply. Who is affected: retail holders forced to move funds on a deadline.

stories.label: Every Mac comes with an (undocumented) family member classifier
stories.summary: A researcher found that Apple Intelligence builds an undocumented on-device knowledge graph on every Mac, including a model that classifies which of your contacts are family. Lead with the undocumented part: inference about your relationships that users never asked for and Apple never disclosed. On-device is not the same as consented; 526 points and 313 comments on Hacker News show developers care.

stories.label: Lowering blood pressure after stroke or with diabetes poses challenges, in research and practice
stories.summary: Three trials at the American Heart Association meeting on hypertension in people with diabetes or after a stroke: a simple approach, a workable solution and a neutral finding (spironolactone among them). Lead with the one result that changes practice and give its numbers; the neutral finding matters too, as evidence of what does not work. Hypertension is the leading preventable killer worldwide, and cheap generic drugs are the stake.

stories.label: Pakistan Information Commission seeks disclosure of travel allowances, perks and expenses of NA committees
stories.summary: Pakistan's Information Commission ordered the National Assembly Secretariat to disclose the travel allowances, perks and expenses of the chairs and members of its standing committees. Lead with the precedent: a right-to-information order aimed at parliament itself. Note whether the secretariat has a deadline and what it has refused before.

stories.label: Iran, Russia stressed deepening security, defense cooperation
stories.summary: Iran's new Supreme National Security Council secretary, Mohsen Rezaei, met Vladimir Putin, and Iran's ambassador says they agreed to deepen security and defence ties and the North–South Transport Corridor. Attribute to Iranian state agency Mehr. Lead with the timing: on the day the US moved to blockade Iran's land and Caspian routes, Tehran's security chief is in Moscow discussing exactly those routes.

stories.label: Police found three more bodies in Krakow shooter's home -- TV
stories.summary: Material new development on the Krakow Main Square shooting: police found two women and a man dead in the gunman's home, confirmed by Prime Minister Donald Tusk, raising the toll from six to nine. Lead with the new toll and Tusk's confirmation; attribute to Polsat via Russian state agency TASS. Do not retell the square attack beyond one line.

stories.label: Paraguay's new president Pedro Alliana
stories.summary: A bank failure toppled a president: Congress impeached Santiago Peña over the collapse of Ueno Bank, which had grown on regulatory favours and public-sector deposits during his term, and Vice President Pedro Alliana has taken office. Lead with the mechanism — state money parked in a politically connected bank, then lost — and who pays: depositors and the public purse. The structural why: ex-president Horacio Cartes, sanctioned by the US for corruption, uses the crisis to claw back control of the ruling Colorado Party. Datelined Asunción.

stories.label: Deadly shooting in popular Krakow tourist spot
stories.summary: A gunman drove into Kraków's historic Main Square and fired at random, killing six people and wounding about 15; police arrested him. Lead with the dead and the count's uncertainty (sources range 5-6), and that mass shootings are rare in Poland, which has among the EU's strictest gun-licensing regimes — so how the attacker was armed is the question to answer. Report only what police have confirmed about motive. Datelined Kraków.

stories.label: 'Everything must change,' Mélenchon tells supporters at rally
stories.summary: Jean-Luc Mélenchon unveiled a 'revolutionary programme' before 20,000 supporters near Paris, riding a wave of protests into the presidential race. Lead with what the programme would actually change — the economy, NATO membership — and the structural why: France's two poll leaders are now the far left and the far right, the centre that ran the state is hollowed out, and a heavily indebted country's creditors are watching. Datelined Le Bourget.

stories.label: In Jericho, Israeli Settlers Violently Seize and Occupy Palestinian Homes
stories.summary: Israeli settlers have forcibly taken over Palestinian homes inside the city of Jericho — not an outlying hamlet but a Palestinian Authority-run city in the occupied West Bank — with soldiers present. Lead with the families thrown out and how many homes, and the escalation: dispossession has moved from the hills and Area C into a Palestinian city itself. Name who protected the takeover and who has done nothing to reverse it. Datelined Jericho.

stories.label: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo becomes largest in country's history - WHO
stories.summary: The WHO says the DR Congo's Ebola outbreak is now the largest in the country's history: 10,668 confirmed cases and 5,198 deaths as of 3 November, across 67 health zones in eight provinces. Lead with the toll — roughly half of the confirmed sick have died — and the spread, then the mechanism: why containment failed (conflict in the east, funding cuts to response, vaccine reach) and which neighbours are on alert. Datelined Kinshasa.

stories.label: Russia upgrades Abu Dhabi delegation as Zelenskyy warns Trump's plan is dangerous
stories.summary: New since our 11-06 story on the Abu Dhabi talks: the Kremlin has upgraded its team to senior diplomats, military officers and intelligence chiefs, while Zelenskyy publicly calls the US plan dangerous. Lead with the upgrade — Moscow signalling it expects to negotiate terms, not just talk — set against Kyiv's warning, and what Ukraine says the plan would cost it. Datelined Abu Dhabi.

stories.label: Yemeni military coducts 6 operations deep inside Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: The Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claims six missile and drone operations against 'strategic sites' deep inside Saudi Arabia, reportedly including Saudi Aramco facilities. Attribute every claim: this is Iranian state news agency Mehr relaying the Houthis, with no independent confirmation in the feed. Lead with what was claimed hit, then the stakes — a reopened Yemen–Saudi front during the Iran war, with Syrian advisers already on Saudi soil (our 11-06 story) — and what it means for Brent crude if Aramco sites are hit. Datelined Sanaa.

stories.label: U.S. Treasury moves to cut off crypto exchange MEXC over $16 billion in alleged illicit flows
stories.summary: FinCEN is moving to cut crypto exchange MEXC off from the US financial system, alleging it handled at least $16 billion tied to Iran, Russia and cybercrime; the order bites 30 days after Federal Register publication. Lead with the $16 billion and the tool — a primary-money-laundering designation that forces banks to sever ties — and who it lands on: the exchange's users and the sanctions-evasion route for Tehran and Moscow. MEXC says it operates normally. Mention bitcoin only if the source ties the order to a price move.

stories.label: BIO joins the legal fight against Medicare pilot that ties drug prices to peer countries
stories.summary: The biotech industry's lobby, BIO, has sued to block GLOBE, a Medicare pilot that pegs US drug prices to what peer countries pay. Lead with the paradox STAT reports: the pilot itself saves little, but the industry is fighting it for the precedent — international reference pricing would end the arrangement in which Americans pay several times what other rich countries do for the same medicine. Name who pays now and who funds the suit. Datelined Washington.

stories.label: Gnosis Pay breach exposes card numbers, home addresses and linked crypto wallets
stories.summary: Crypto debit-card provider Gnosis Pay disclosed a breach exposing card numbers, home addresses and the crypto wallets linked to them — weeks before it shuts its branded cards on 20 December, and after a $1.5 million exploit in June. Lead with the dangerous combination: a leaked home address tied to a known wallet balance is a map for physical 'wrench attacks' on holders. The structural point: self-custody crypto plugged into card rails inherits the card industry's KYC data honeypot.

stories.label: Two paths, one flux: Trapped ions simulate Aharonov–Bohm interference in a lattice gauge theory
stories.summary: A Nature Physics study used a hybrid trapped-ion quantum computer to reproduce the Aharonov–Bohm effect — a particle 'feeling' a magnetic field it never passes through — inside a simulated lattice gauge theory, the mathematical framework of the forces in the Standard Model. Lead with the effect in plain words, then why it matters: quantum simulators are starting to compute the gauge physics that classical supercomputers cannot. Thin source; the writer should read the Nature Physics paper.

stories.label: Qeshm island and Hormuz hit, as mediators try to prevent US-Iran escalation
stories.summary: New development since the UKMTO tally: the US struck Qeshm island again after more ships were attacked, and Iran's navy says a tanker that switched off its transponder hit a mine and caught fire in a 'prohibited' zone of the eastern strait. Lead with the strikes and the mine, then the mediators racing to stop a wider war; name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude. Iran's mine claim comes from its navy via Mehr (state media) and must be attributed.

stories.label: Kyiv Faces Russian Missile Barrage, Hits Saratov Oil Refinery
stories.summary: Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles and 172 drones at Kyiv's energy facilities and bridges, and only 4 of the missiles were shot down, while Ukraine hit the Saratov oil refinery. Lead with the ballistic interception gap and civilians facing winter without power; the mechanism is a two-way energy war while the Abu Dhabi talks run. Mention Brent crude only if the refinery strike moved fuel supply.

stories.label: Pro-Russian hackers leak Italian foreign minister's data on dark web
stories.summary: Antonio Tajani's personal data was dumped on the dark web and Meloni blames pro-Russian hackers; Tajani says the attack is still going on. Lead with a sitting G7 foreign minister doxxed, then the mechanism: hack-and-leak against officials of a government that backs Ukraine. Attribution is Rome's claim, not yet a forensic finding.

stories.label: 'Run bulldozer over me...': Mamata lashes out at BJP over attack on Abhishek Banerjee's home
stories.summary: After losing power in West Bengal, Mamata Banerjee says BJP supporters attacked her nephew Abhishek Banerjee's house and blocked Kali Puja at her Kalighat home. Lead with the attack, then the pattern: violence against the losing side after Bengal's elections, now aimed at the former ruling family. Keep both sides' claims attributed.

stories.label: Donald Trump teases more firings, defends Pete Hegseth
stories.summary: After the midterm defeat, which voters and Vance tied to the Iran war and fuel prices, Trump promises 'a few changes' but keeps Defense Secretary Hegseth, the man running that war. Lead with who stays: the shake-up after Miller replaced Wiles spares the architect of the policy voters punished. Don't repeat the Miller story.

stories.label: Houston mayor curbs cooperation of US city's police with ICE
stories.summary: Texas's largest city will stop referring people stopped for minor traffic violations to ICE, which puts Mayor Whitmire in conflict with Governor Abbott and state law. Lead with the traffic-stop pipeline to deportation that is being closed, and who it protects; the days after the midterms test how far cities will go.

stories.label: Govt announces auto policy with focus on cheaper vehicles, EVs
stories.summary: Pakistan's new auto policy aims at cheaper cars and electric vehicles in a market long held by a few Japanese assemblers behind high tariffs. Lead with what changes for buyers in price, tariffs and localisation, and tie it to the fuel import bill that the Iran war pushed up.

stories.label: British soldier ignored order to pull his SIM card, then got blackmailed
stories.summary: A British soldier on NATO's Estonian flank, 90 miles from Russia, kept his SIM card in against orders, was sextorted and was court-martialed, as an Estonian newspaper revealed. Lead with the phone as the soft spot of a forward deployment: the attack surface is the device, not the base.

stories.label: The migration that transformed Africa's languages, genes, and cultures
stories.summary: Ancient DNA and archaeology are now showing how Bantu speakers spread across much of sub-Saharan Africa, carrying iron-working and farming as far as Great Zimbabwe. Lead with the newest genetic finding in the piece: Africans as the authors of one of humanity's largest migrations, not the setting for one.

stories.label: No, a strike on Iran's nukes can't cook Pakistan, Afghanistan
stories.summary: A viral map claims fallout from strikes on Iran's nuclear sites would reach Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan and Afghanistan. Dawn explains the physics: an enrichment site is not a reactor core, and its inventory of fission products is tiny. Lead with the real hazard (chemical UF6 and local contamination) set against the imagined plume.

stories.label: Big Tech, AI, and the quiet expansion of digital surveillance in Nigeria
stories.summary: Global Voices maps how Big Tech platforms and AI systems are expanding data collection in Nigeria beyond what users expect or understand, under a data-protection regime that is weakly enforced. Lead with the most concrete case of collection the piece documents, and who profits from it. The structural why: Africa's largest online market is being mined for data under rules written for it but not enforced. Datelined Lagos.

stories.label: US offers $20 million reward for information on Iran's nuclear program
stories.summary: The State Department's Rewards for Justice offer — $20 million and possible relocation for information on Iran's nuclear programme — is an admission: Washington says the IAEA has lost 'continuity of knowledge' over Iran's production and inventory of key components, and floats their 'possible relocation'. Lead with that: after months of bombing, the US no longer knows where the material is, and is buying informants instead. Explain what continuity of knowledge means in safeguards terms and why inspectors lost it. No regional outlet in the feed carries this. Datelined Washington.

stories.label: Delhi sees 'very poor' air ahead of Diwali, AQI stands at 364
stories.summary: Delhi's AQI hit 364 a day before Diwali, with 22 stations above 400 and PM2.5 the lead pollutant at 53 of 59 monitors, and GRAP Stage III curbs — construction bans, vehicle limits — now in force across the capital region. Lead with who breathes it: some 30 million people, with outdoor workers and the poor least able to shelter. The structural why: the same seasonal mix of stubble burning, traffic and still winter air returns every year, and the response is still emergency curbs rather than a fix. Datelined Delhi.

stories.label: Why Israel's Ex-Army Chief's Next Mission Could Be Mission Impossible
stories.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, the former army chief, is all but certain on Sunday to be handed the mandate to form Israel's next government after a majority of Knesset members recommended him, ending Netanyahu's hold on the premiership. Lead with the fact of the handover, then the arithmetic: which parties recommended him, the coalition he needs and the obstacles. Hold him to his record — he was chief of staff during the 2014 Gaza war and authored the 'Dahiya doctrine' of disproportionate force against civilian infrastructure — and say what his government would mean for Gaza and the West Bank. Report, don't editorialise; this is the news, not the NYT's analysis frame. Datelined Jerusalem.

stories.label: Amnesty condemns violent attacks on Atiku campaign convoy in Kebbi
stories.summary: Attackers set on the campaign convoys of Atiku Abubakar's African Democratic Congress in Kebbi State on Thursday, and Amnesty International warns of a rising wave of political repression ahead of Nigeria's elections. Lead with what happened in Kebbi — who was hurt, who is accused — then the pattern Amnesty documents: opposition campaigns obstructed while police look away. The accountability question is whether anyone is charged. Datelined Birnin Kebbi.

stories.label: Bushra Bibi approaches IHC over worsening eyesight, seeks treatment from doctors of her choice
stories.summary: Bushra Bibi, Imran Khan's wife, jailed alongside him, has petitioned the Islamabad High Court for an immediate eye examination and the right to see doctors of her choice at her own expense, citing deteriorating eyesight. Lead with the request: a prisoner asking a court for permission to pay for her own medical care. The structural why: medical access has become a lever over Pakistan's most prominent political prisoners, and the courts are where it is contested. Datelined Islamabad.

stories.label: US urges China to honour Busan trade deal commitments
stories.summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent and trade envoy Greer met Vice Premier He Lifeng and pressed Beijing to implement the Busan truce immediately — the deal that traded US tariff and chip-export relief for Chinese commitments on soybeans, rare-earth exports and fentanyl. Lead with what China has not delivered and what the US has threatened to restore if it doesn't; the leverage on each side is rare earths versus tariffs. Note the yuan only if the source ties a move to it.

stories.label: Políticos, empresários e a Meta estão por trás dos boicotes a eleitores do PT nas redes
stories.summary: Agência Pública traces the social-media campaigns calling for boycotts of businesses and workers who voted for Lula's PT to named legislators, business owners and Meta's platforms, and Brazil's Labour Prosecutor's Office (MPT) is now investigating both the politicians and the company. Lead with the mechanism: how a platform's tools were used to organise economic punishment of voters, and why a labour prosecutor, not an election court, is the one acting. Datelined São Paulo.

stories.label: 存储风暴压顶，小众手机「在劫难逃」
stories.summary: The inside view from China's tech press: the surge in memory-chip prices, as DRAM and NAND output is diverted to AI servers, is squeezing China's niche phone makers out of the market, since they lack the volume to lock in supply. Lead with which brands are cutting models or exiting and by how much their memory costs rose. The structural why: the AI build-out is pricing consumer electronics out of components — and it frames this week's fall in SK Hynix shares, a bet on that boom. Datelined Beijing.

stories.label: Medical services company settles with 4 states over 2023 hack of sensitive patient records
stories.summary: Attorneys general in Connecticut, New Jersey, New York and Michigan settled with the transcription, coding and imaging subsidiaries of Nevada-based Perry Johnson Companies over a 2023 breach of sensitive patient records. Lead with how many patients were exposed, what was taken and what the settlement costs and requires, set against the three years it took. The structural why: the medical back-office contractors patients never chose hold their records, and state AGs, not a federal regulator, are the ones enforcing.

stories.label: Democracy falters in Tanzania
stories.summary: A Tanzanian court jailed Tundu Lissu, the country's most influential opposition leader and Chadema's chairman, for incitement, while lifting the treason charge that carried the death penalty. Lead with the swap: dropping the capital charge still takes Samia Suluhu Hassan's main challenger out of politics. The structural why is the wider African pattern of opposition leaders removed through treason and incitement trials rather than at the ballot box. Datelined Dar es Salaam.

stories.label: Hospital Escuela: más de 6,000 pacientes esperan cirugía y el plan para reducir la mora avanza con apenas 405 operaciones en privados
stories.summary: More than 6,000 patients are waiting for surgery at Honduras's largest public hospital, the Hospital Escuela, and over 1,000 elective operations piled up during 49 days of doctors' assemblies. The government's fix — paying private hospitals up to 110,000 lempiras per operation through a 500-million-lempira trust — had delivered only 405 procedures by July, and how the trust's money is spent is not disclosed. Lead with 6,000 against 405: the poor wait while public money flows to private clinics with no accounting. Datelined Tegucigalpa.

stories.label: UKMTO says 11 ships attacked in week to 4 Nov in Hormuz, Arabian Gulf
stories.summary: UK Maritime Trade Operations counted 11 attacks on commercial shipping in the seven days to November 4 — eight in the Strait of Hormuz, three in the Arabian Gulf — and three vessels sunk. Lead with the weekly toll and the sinkings: the first official tally after the Velos Sapphire death shows the strait is now a battlefield, not a risk premium, and the seafarers crewing it bear the cost. Name the series: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, and Brent crude.

stories.label: 'E20 turned into 420': Rahul Gandhi alleges petrol samples from Karnataka exceed 20% ethanol limit
stories.summary: Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi published lab tests of petrol from seven Karnataka districts in which 11 samples exceeded the 20% ethanol cap of India's E20 mandate. Lead with the lab figures and who supplies the fuel — the state refiners Indian Oil, BPCL and HPCL. The structural why: the ethanol mandate saves India oil imports and pays sugar growers, while motorists carry the engine wear and mileage loss, and nobody independently tests the blend at the pump. Present it as an allegation backed by tests, with the refiners' response. Datelined Bengaluru.

stories.label: Ex-Everbright Executive and Wife Took 4.29 Million Yuan in Salary Bribes
stories.summary: China's top judicial authorities released case details showing a former China Everbright Bank executive and his wife collected 4.29 million yuan ($640,000) as salaries for nominal jobs at companies he helped win loans. Lead with the mechanism: a bribe paid as a payroll line, a disguise that prosecutors are now publicising as a pattern. The structural why is Beijing's anti-graft campaign in state finance turning to hidden forms of payment between state-bank lenders and their borrowers.

stories.label: US Believes Woman Close to Nvidia CEO Was a China Spy, NYT Says
stories.summary: US intelligence officials told the Trump administration that Alice Huang, a woman close to Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, was a Chinese intelligence asset, and the House Select Committee on China has asked him to a briefing on his contacts with her and Nvidia's counter-espionage protocols. Lead with the stakes: the head of the company whose chips sit at the centre of US export controls on China is now himself a counter-intelligence question. Attribute the claim to US officials, as reported by the NYT. Datelined Washington.

stories.label: 刚刚，OpenAI被曝又拿730亿，估值超8.3万亿
stories.summary: OpenAI closed a first tranche of about $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, from a round it cut from a planned $30 billion at $1.4 trillion to at most $20 billion after the AI-stock rout. Investors in Anthropic's planned IPO have meanwhile marked it down from $1.4-1.5 trillion to $1.1-1.3 trillion, and Blackstone has warned its debt may rate as junk against about $895 billion in compute and lease commitments. Lead with the shrinking round: the AI selloff has reached the private labs, whose spending depends on capital that is now harder to raise. Datelined San Francisco.
